subject.title: Browser-opened temporary tabs/windows should close automatically after task completion

question: Should OpenClaw close primary-agent run-owned browser tabs at task completion by default, and which user actions should preserve a tab?
rationale: Current code intentionally keeps active primary-session tabs reusable, so changing the default requires maintainer intent on task terminal events, tab ownership, and user-preservation rules.

options.title: Run-owned cleanup with preservation
options.body: Track tabs created during a primary-agent run and close only those not explicitly foregrounded, pinned, or requested to be kept.

options.title: Keep idle/cap behavior only
options.body: Treat the current reusable-tab model as sufficient and close this direction as not planned if task-end cleanup is too surprising.

options.title: Opt-in strict cleanup
options.body: Add a documented opt-in cleanup mode while preserving current reusable-tab behavior by default.

recommendation.title: Run-owned cleanup with preservation
recommendation.body: Track tabs created during a primary-agent run and close only those not explicitly foregrounded, pinned, or requested to be kept.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across idle tab cleanup, lifecycle cleanup helpers, and peer-scoped reset cleanup.
